what_this_is: The Workshop row for the tool in tools/read-a-list-view: one page of what a person's list or saved view shows, read from their records through their own door, and the refresh that writes a list's row sources into those records.

payload.label: Read a page of one of my lists or saved views, or refresh its row sources
payload.job: Read one page of what one of my lists or saved views shows, from my records, or refresh a list's row sources (a folder of documents, for one) into its records
payload.description: Reads the list (or the saved view and its list) through the person's door, from records only: the list's rows are the records of its row type, and each row source's rows are among them, written there by the last refresh (row id <source>~<its id>), so a read runs no tool. A page holds `limit` rows (read_page_rows when left out, never more than rows_per_read) and answers `next` while more remain. A view with rules keeps the rows its rules keep, decided in the same process by the rule filter of tools/formulas, ordered by its sort. With `refresh` it runs the tool each row source names (read-data/list-view.json), reads the whole source, and writes its rows as the list's records: only the rows that changed, removing the rows the source no longer has, in bounded writes. A source with more than rows_per_read rows, a source no tool serves, or a source that answers no rows is refused and nothing of it is written.

config.description: The person's door config file (the README describes its keys).

list.description: The list's id; give this or view.

view.description: The saved view's record id; give this or list.

after.description: The `next` of the page before; left out for the first page.

refresh.description: A list's id: run its row sources and write their rows as its records, instead of reading a page.

source_ids.description: For refresh, only these declared source ids; every selected source is read completely before its stale rows can be removed. CLI: --sources as a JSON array. Unselected source records are never read, run, written or removed.

output_schema.description: A page { list, fields, rows: [{ id, record_id, values, title, source? }], next, complete, of? }, or for a refresh { list, sources: [{ source, rows, written, removed, unchanged, refused }] }, as JSON; exit 2 with the reason on standard error.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout, and reads their lists through their own door with their own key. Use --view instead of --list for a saved view, and --refresh with a list's id when they want its row sources read again: a refresh is the only thing that runs the source tools. Show the rows as a table of the list's fields, and read the next page with `next` until it is null when they want every row.

provenance.source: Written for the Workshop: a list read that pages across a list's own records and its row sources, in the way a database view joins its tables
